1.

The present petition has been filed with the assertion that the petitioner herein had purchased the land in Revenue Survey No.509 (Old Revenue Survey No.376-B located at village Motoraypura,

sentences.text: Taluka: Nandod, District: Narmada admeasuring 5126 sq.meters, out of the total area of 7891 sq.meters, vide registered sale deed dated 22.07.2011.
The Revenue Entry No.1659 came to be mutated on 26.07.2011.
Initially, the said entry was cancelled on the premise that the certificate of the petitioner being an original agriculturist was not submitted.
However, another Revenue Entry No.1664 came to be mutated on 14.11.2011 and came to be later NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/240/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined certified on 25.01.2012.

The land in question was acquired vide Notifications dated 06.05.2010 and 05.05.2011 under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short as "the Act' 1894); respectively, for the purpose of widening of the State Highway No.5 (Rajpipla-Gaurdashwar Road).

It is stated that initially there were 10 co-owners of the land in question, however, they had later relinquished their rights in the land in question and it was absolutely vested in the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner,
namely, Mr. Gohil Gopalsinh Ganpatsinh.

A Revenue Entry No.1650 dated 03.06.2011 had been made in this regard, which was certified on 14.07.2011.
2.
It is then stated that the petitioner was not aware of the acquisition proceedings as the seller did not inform him about the same.

An award dated 24.08.2012 was passed by the Assistant Collector,
Narmada- Rajpipla and the vendor, namely Mr. Gohil Gopalsinh Ganpatsinh had accepted the total compensation amount of the land in question vide cheque dated 10.06.2016.

It is then stated that one Mr. Balvantsinh Himmatsinh Gohil, whose name was reflected in the Revenue records with respect to Survey No.376-A had preferred application under Section 18 seeking Reference, wherein Mr. Gohil Gopalsinh Ganpatsinh, the vendor of the sale deed dated 22.07.2011 executed in favour NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/240/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined of the petitioner,
as well as the petitioner filed applications for impleadment in LAR Case No.49 of 2013.

3. Vide judgement and order dated 12.09.2017 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Narmada,
both the applications were rejected giving liberty to the applicants to agitate their rights and interests by approaching the Special Land Acquisition Officer seeking reference of the dispute to the competent authority.
It is submitted that LAR Case No.49 of 2013 filed by the owners of Survey No.376-A has been allowed in part vide judgement and order dated 03.10.2017.

It is also stated that the vendor had preferred Regular Civil Suit No.60 of 2014 seeking for cancellation of the sale deed in favour of the petitioner and with the relief of declaration and injunction.
The said suit has been dismissed vide judgement and order dated 20.10.2022 passed by the Senior Civil Judge, Narmada.

4. With these facts, it is vehemently contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner, who is a purchaser of the property in question had no option but to approach the Collector for making reference of the dispute pertaining to the apportionment of the compensation by invoking provisions of Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 ( in short as 'the Act'1894)
and/or Section 76 of the Right to Fair Compensation Act, 2013 , as the dispute is with NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/240/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined respect to apportionment of compensation for the land bearing Revenue Survey No.509 (Old Survey No.376-B), admeasuring 5126 sq.meters as per the award dated 03.10.2017 passed in LAR Case No.49 of 2013

. 
5. In essence, the petitioner is seeking disbursement of compensation for an area of 5126 sq.meters (Old Survey No.376-B, Revenue Survey No.509, which according to him, was included in Land Mafatlal Chandulal Chauhan vs State Of Gujarat on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158715342/
2 Reference Case No.49 of 2013 and enhanced compensation which was granted to the claimant vide judgement and order dated 03.10.2017.

sentences.text:
It is contended that in LAR No.49 of 2013, the claimant therein sought compensation both with respect to Survey No.376-A and 376- B, whereas 376-B was the land belonging to the petitioner,as he had purchased the same vide registered sale deed dated 22.07.2011.
6.

By placing Section 30 of the Act'1894, it is contended that all disputes pertaining to the compensation or even entitlement to it are required to be referred to the competent Court of Civil jurisdiction by the Special Land Acquisition Officer/ Collector.

As the petitioner is raising the dispute with regard to the receipt of compensation by the respondent No.6, namely Mr. Balvantsinh Himmatsinh Gohil in the reference under Section 18 filed by him and the application filed by the petitioner has been rejected on the ground that the petitioner NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/240/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined may raise a dispute before the competent authority, the Collector/ Special Land Acquisition Officer was obliged to refer the dispute to the competent Court.

It was argued that the only prayer made in the writ petition is to issue directions to the Special Land Acquisition Officer to refer the dispute for adjudication before the competent Civil Court, by deciding the application under Section 30 moved by the petitioner herein,
which deserves consideration.

7. Reliance is placed on the decision of this Court in Mathubhai Samjibhai Raiyani vs. State of Gujarat, 2015(O) JX(Gujarat) 389, and the decisions of the Apex Court in the case of Rameshchand and other vs. Tanmay Developers private Limited, 2017(13) SCC 715 and Patel Kodarbhai Mohanbhai vs. Sonata Ceramica Private Limited, 2022(14) Scale 193, to contend that in all these matters the Court has observed that the rights and contentions of the parties can be decided under Section 30 of the Act'1894.

sentences.text:
8. Taking note of the above contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner, we may note the provisions of Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, which reads as under:
"30. Dispute as to apportionment. - When the amount of compensation has been settled under section 11, if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the same or any part thereof, or as to the persons to whom the same or any part thereof, is payable, the Collector may refer NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/240/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined such dispute to the decision of the Court."
9.

A bare reading of Section 30 indicates that on settlement of the amount of compensation under Section 11, if any dispute arose as to the apportionment of the compensation so determined or any part thereof, or there is a dispute as to the person to whom the sum or in part thereof is payable, the Collector has to refer such dispute to the decision of the Court.

10. The reference, thus, made under Section 30 of the Act'1894 is confined to the question of apportionment of the compensation amongst various claimants of the compensation amount which is determined under Section 11 of the Act'1894.

Mafatlal Chandulal Chauhan vs State Of Gujarat on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158715342/
3 11.

sentences.text: In the instant case, it is admitted that the petitioner has not received compensation under the original award passed under Section 11 of the Act, 1894, which according to him has been received by the vendor vide Cheque dated 10.06.2017, even after the sale deed dated 22.07.2011 was executed in favour of the petitioner herein.

We may note that it is sought to be submitted that the co-owners of the land in question of Survey No.376-B had relinquished their rights and it was absolutely vested with the vendor of the sale deed dated 22.07.20211 executed in favour of the petitioner.

As per the statement made in the writ petition, the total area of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/240/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined Survey No.376-B was 7891 sq.meters, out of which 5126 sq.meters is the land in dispute.

The respondent No.6, namely Mr. Balvantsinh Himmatsinh Gohil had filed reference case seeking enhancement of compensation both for Survey Nos.376-A area 00-38-13 sq.meters and 376-B, area 00-51-26 sq.meters.

The contention, thus, is that the enhanced compensation for an area of 5126 sq.meters has been obtained by the respondent No.6 Mr.
Balvantsinh Himmatsinh Gohil and the compensation under the original award has been received by the vendor, namely Mr.Gohil Gopalsinh Ganpatsinh.

The result is that the petitioner did not receive any money for the acquired land though registered sale deed dated 20.07.2011 had been executed in his favour by Mr.Gohil Gopalsinh Ganpatsinh, son of Ganpatsinh Gohil.
It is also stated that the petitioner was never informed about the acquisition proceedings by the vendor.

12. From the above facts, it is evident that the dispute sought to be raised before us is about the entitlement of the petitioner to receive compensation under the original award and the enhanced compensation under the reference award dated 03.10.2017 passed in LAR No.49 of 2013 in favour of the respondent No.6.

The question as to whether the petitioner is entitled to receive compensation,
which has already been NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/240/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined disbursed to the previous owners of the land in question, cannot be decided by seeking reference to the dispute under Section 30 of the Act' 1894, which is confined to the issue pertaining to the apportionment of the compensation amongst various claimants.

13. The appropriate remedy for the petitioner is to file a Civil Suit seeking for declaration and adjudication of his right to receive compensation of the acquired land based on the sale deed dated 22.07.2011 as also the enhanced compensation under the Land Acquisition Reference No.49 of 2013.

The reliance is placed on the decision of this Court and the Apex Court to assert that the appropriate remedy for the petitioner is to approach the Collector under Section 30 of the Act' 1894,
is found to be misconceived.

14. Even otherwise, the prayer made in the writ petition to seek reference of the dispute pertaining to apportionment of compensation as per the award dated 03.10.2017 passed in LAR Case No.49 of 2013 cannot be made, under Section 30 of the Act'1894,which only talks of a reference of the dispute pertaining to apportionment of compensation under the award declared under Section 11 of the Act'
1894, for the simple reason that any order passed under Section 18 of the Act' 1894 becomes a decree of the Civil Court.

The Collector has no power to make any reference under Section 30 to NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/240/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined refer as to who would be entitled to disbursement of compensation on the enhanced compensation granted by the Civil Court under Section 30 of the Act' 1894.

A decree passed by the Civil Court in the shape of the reference Court award dated 03.10.2017 in LAR Case No.49 of 2013 cannot be modified or altered Mafatlal Chandulal Chauhan vs State Of Gujarat on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158715342/
4 by making a reference under Section 30 of the Act' 1894.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. The argument of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has become remediless because of the rejection of his application by the reference Court in the proceedings under Section 18 of the Act' 1894, is of no consequence, inasmuch as, the civil remedy to approach the competent Court is still available to the petitioner.
16. With the above, present petition is dismissed being devoid of merits.
